comparison_rule: Learned model and baseline are compared on the paired set: the held-out rows where BOTH produced a forecast. On each paired row the learned model 'wins' when |actual - learned| < |actual - baseline|, 'loses' when it is greater, and the row is a 'tie' when they are equal. win_proportion = wins / paired. Differences are learned - baseline (negative = smaller learned error). No threshold is applied, no winner is declared, and no number is a verdict.

limitations: Same source: the held-out months come from the same two Portuguese hotels (2015-2017) whose earlier months the model was fitted on. Nothing here establishes generalisation to other hotels or production accuracy.
Not pristine: the Stage 6.3 backtest refitted the same method across these months and its results are published. No setting was tuned on them, but they are not unseen.
Seasonal mismatch: validation is November-April and test is April-August; the two are reported separately and are not interchangeable.
Two hotels: the cross-hotel experiment has two directions and no third hotel; it measures transfer between these two, not to hotels in general.

Weak range untested: no validation or test target is below forty room nights (0 of 590 rows; counted from the targets before any scoring), so the served model's known weak range (about 165.83 for small histories) is not exercised here and its breakdown reports no metric.
Duplicates: 31,994 duplicate source rows retained by Stage 6.2 inflate demand consistently; every figure inherits that uncertainty.
Point forecasts only: no interval, no uncertainty quantification, no capacity cap.
